_note: Everything in this file is OUTSIDE the atlas's evidence. The walks report what sources describe. These are the answers people have proposed to the question the accounts stop at, and each one is named, attributed and labelled by what kind of claim it is. Nothing here is a finding and nothing here is presented as one.
heading: The account stops here
lede: Past this point the atlas stops reporting. What follows is what people have proposed, labelled so you always know which kind of claim you are reading.
back_note: What this source says happened next.
on_note: Twelve proposals, from religion, science and elsewhere.
root: What happens if you do not come back?
root_note: No account answers this: everyone who could report has come back. Everything below the root is a proposal, not a finding.

domains.name: Religion
domains.note: Teaching about what is the case, held on authority rather than offered as evidence. Four of these traditions never met and still agree on a surprising amount, which is the reason to draw them side by side.

domains.name: Science
domains.note: Two very different things sit under this word here. One branch has laboratory evidence for its mechanism and predicts that nothing continues. The other starts from well-tested physics and then takes a step the physics does not take. Keeping them on separate limbs is the point.

domains.name: Other
domains.note: Proposals that are neither revealed nor measured. Right now that is one limb, Greek philosophy; it is where anything else would go.

families.name: Abrahamic
families.note: A resurrection, a reckoning, and a place entered rather than a state attained. Judaism belongs on this limb and is not here yet: the atlas has no citable path for it.

families.name: Dharmic
families.note: Not one destination but a cycle, and the aim is to stop going round it. Death is a door in the middle of the process rather than the end of it.

families.name: Ancient Egypt and Iran
families.note: The two oldest surviving systems that weigh a life and then sort it. Both put a balance at the hinge, and the Egyptian one is the oldest description of the shape that survives anywhere.

families.name: Indigenous and Pacific
families.note: The route runs through real, named geography rather than a separate world, and the departure point is a place you can stand in today.

families.name: Neuroscience
families.note: The default position, and the only branch on this tree whose mechanism has been demonstrated in a laboratory. What it predicts is that there is nothing further to walk into.

families.name: Physics
families.note: Each of these begins in established physics and ends in a claim the physics does not make. None of the physicists cited said their result was evidence that a person survives, and the cards say where the step happens.

families.name: Greek philosophy
families.note: Rebirth argued rather than revealed, with the choice of the next life placed squarely on the chooser. Plato has the interpreter say it outright: virtue is not assigned.

paths.name: Into the city
paths.claim: The righteous are washed and brought inside a city of gold.
paths.cite: Apocalypse of Paul, sections 22-23, 4th century, M. R. James translation, 1924. Compare Revelation 21:10-21.

stages.label: Washed in the lake
stages.text: Michael washes the repentant in the lake Acherusa, whose water is whiter than milk, and so brings them in to the city of Christ.

stages.label: Twelve walls
stages.text: The city is all of gold, with twelve walls, twelve towers and twelve gates, ringed by four rivers: honey, milk, oil and wine.

stages.label: No night there
stages.text: In Revelation's version of the same city there is no temple in it and no sun, because the glory of God lightens it, and the gates are never shut, for there is no night.

paths.name: The bar, the balance and the bridge
paths.claim: The dead wait behind a barrier until the resurrection, are weighed, and cross over the fire to two gardens.
paths.note: What the Qur'an describes of paradise is gardens, shade, fountains, fruit, couches, four rivers and companions. Two things usually attached to it are not in it. The bridge over hell is not Qur'anic: Sale notes at 19:71 that some commentators read the narrow bridge into that verse, crediting al-Baydawi, but the verse itself says only that all shall approach the fire. And the figure of seventy-two companions is not in the Qur'an at all; searching a complete translation for the number finds it only in notes about Noah's ark and Jacob's family. It belongs to the hadith literature rather than to scripture, and this atlas has not verified its grading there, so it makes no claim about it.
paths.cite: The Koran, George Sale translation, 1734, in the standard 1892 printing; suras 23:99-103, 19:71, 47:15, 55:46-76, 37:48-49 and 18:31. Sale's own footnotes, which name his authorities, are quoted where they are quoted.

stages.label: Behind them, a bar
stages.text: When death overtakes a man he says: O Lord, suffer me to return to life, that I may do that which is right. By no means. Verily these are the words which he shall speak: but behind them there shall be a bar, until the day of resurrection.

stages.label: The balances
stages.text: When the trumpet is sounded there shall be no relation between them which shall be regarded on that day. They whose balances shall be heavy with good works shall be happy; but they whose balances shall be light have lost their souls.

stages.label: Over the fire
stages.text: The believers must also pass by or through hell, but the fire will be damped and the flames abated, so as not to hurt them. Some suppose the words intend no more than the passage over the narrow bridge, which is laid over hell.

stages.label: Two gardens
stages.text: For him who dreadeth the tribunal of his Lord are prepared two gardens, planted with shady trees. In each of them shall be two fountains flowing. In each of them shall there be of every fruit two kinds.

stages.label: Four rivers, and no excess of heat or cold
stages.text: Therein are rivers of incorruptible water, and rivers of milk the taste whereof changeth not, and rivers of wine pleasant unto those who drink, and rivers of clarified honey. They repose on couches lined with thick silk interwoven with gold.

stages.label: The companions, as the text has them
stages.text: Having large black eyes, and kept in pavilions from public view. Near them shall lie the virgins of paradise, refraining their looks from beholding any besides their spouses. Therein shall they delight themselves, lying on green cushions and beautiful carpets.

paths.name: Into another body
paths.claim: The self is not destroyed with the body; it takes up another.
paths.cite: Bhagavad Gita 2:20-22; Katha Upanishad I.2. Public-domain translations: K. T. Telang, Sacred Books of the East vol. 8, 1882; F. Max Muller, SBE vol. 15, 1884.

stages.label: It is not slain
stages.text: The Gita's claim is flat: it is not born, nor does it ever die; it is not slain when the body is slain. Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it.

stages.label: Worn-out garments
stages.text: As a man casts off worn-out garments and takes new ones, so the dweller in the body casts off worn-out bodies and enters into others.

stages.label: Or no return at all
stages.text: The aim is not another body but the end of needing one. The Upanishads call the escape from the cycle release, and describe it as knowing rather than going anywhere.

paths.name: The bardo, and a womb door
paths.claim: Forty-nine days in an intermediate state, then rebirth, unless the clear light is recognised.
paths.cite: Bardo Thodol (the Tibetan Book of the Dead), 14th century, W. Y. Evans-Wentz translation, 1927.

stages.label: The clear light
stages.text: At the first moment of death the clear light of reality dawns. Recognise it and the sequence ends there. Almost nobody recognises it, and so the journey goes on.

stages.label: Peaceful, then wrathful
stages.text: Over the following weeks the peaceful forms appear, then the wrathful ones. The teaching insists repeatedly that they are the mind's own projections and not external beings.

stages.label: The womb door
stages.text: Drawn towards a birth, the consciousness is urged to close the womb door, and failing that to choose well. Forty-nine days is the outer limit before rebirth.

paths.name: A homestead for ever
paths.claim: Found true in the balance, the dead are given land to farm in perpetuity.
paths.cite: The Book of the Dead, Chapter XV and the judgment scene, E. A. Wallis Budge translation of the Papyrus of Ani, 1895.

stages.label: No wickedness found
stages.text: Thoth announces the verdict: the heart has in very truth been weighed, and found true by trial in the Great Balance. There has not been found any wickedness in him.

stages.label: Sekhet-hetepu
stages.text: Horus takes him by the hand and leads him to Osiris, who grants a homestead for ever in Sekhet-hetepu, with wheat and barley for it.

stages.label: Among the followers of Horus
stages.text: The reward is not rest but ordinary work made permanent: fields, grain, and a place among the followers of Horus.

paths.name: The four tracks to Garothman
paths.claim: The good go up by stages: star, moon, sun, and then the all-glorious.
paths.cite: The Book of Arda Viraf, chapters 7-11, Martin Haug translation, 1872.

stages.label: Star, moon, sun
stages.text: The first footstep is the star track, where the pious glitter as stars. The second is the moon track. The third is the radiance they call the highest of the highest.

stages.label: Garothman
stages.text: The fourth footstep is the radiance of Garothman, the all-glorious, where Adar shows the blue water of a large tank and says: this is the water which that wood exuded.

stages.label: Taken by the hand
stages.text: Vohuman rises from a throne made of gold, takes the newcomer's hand, and brings them into the midst of Ohrmazd and the archangels.

paths.name: The leaping-off place
paths.claim: Spirits travel north to the cape and depart from it for the homeland.
paths.cite: The geography as described in the account Michael King recorded, Being Pakeha, 1985, pp. 92-94, quoted in Kellehear A, Journal of Near-Death Studies 2001;20:31-35.

stages.label: North, to the cape
stages.text: The route runs north, river by named river, to Te Rerenga Wairua at Cape Reinga. In the account that this atlas carries, a voice stops the traveller at exactly this point and sends her home.

stages.label: The entrance
stages.text: She performs ablutions, climbs a ledge and dances before the entrance to the underworld. What lies past it is the part her account does not report.

stages.label: Towards the homeland
stages.text: In the tradition the spirits leap from here and travel to the ancestral homeland. That is teaching, not testimony: nobody in this atlas describes the far side of it.

paths.name: Choosing the next life
paths.claim: Souls pick their own next life, drink from the river of Forgetfulness, and are born again.
paths.cite: Plato, Republic X, 617d-621b, Benjamin Jowett translation.

stages.label: The lots are thrown
stages.text: An interpreter throws lots among them and sets out the patterns of lives: tyrannies and exiles, beauty and poverty, animals as well as men. Virtue is not assigned. The responsibility is the chooser's.

stages.label: The river of Unmindfulness
stages.text: They camp on the plain of Forgetfulness beside the river of Unmindfulness, and all are made to drink a measure of its water. Those without sense drink more than the measure.

stages.label: Shot like stars
stages.text: In the middle of the night there is thunder and an earthquake, and they are driven upwards to their birth, suddenly, in all directions, like shooting stars.

paths.name: The last thing a brain does
paths.claim: The experience is produced by a brain under extreme stress, and it stops when the brain does.
paths.cite: Blanke O et al. Stimulating illusory own-body perceptions. Nature 2002;419:269-70. Borjigin J et al. Surge of neurophysiological coherence and connectivity in the dying brain. PNAS 2013;110:14432-7. Vicente R et al. Enhanced interplay of neuronal coherence and coupling in the dying human brain. Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience 2022;14:813531.

stages.label: The seat of it was found
stages.text: Blanke's group stimulated the right temporoparietal junction in a patient being assessed for epilepsy surgery and reliably produced the sensation of leaving the body. The feeling has an address in the brain.

stages.label: A surge, not a signal
stages.text: In dying rats and in dying human brains, researchers recorded a surge of gamma activity and coupling after the heart stopped. A brain going out is not quiet, which is the mechanism this branch rests on.

stages.label: And then nothing
stages.text: On this account there is no further walk, and the honest end of the scene is that it stops. This is the only branch on this page whose mechanism has been demonstrated in a laboratory, and what it predicts is that there is nothing to see.

paths.name: The holographic principle
paths.who: Gerard 't Hooft, Leonard Susskind, Juan Maldacena
paths.claim: What is established: the physics inside a region can be fully described by information on its boundary. What is only proposed: that a life's information therefore persists after the body that carried it.
paths.cite: 't Hooft G. Dimensional reduction in quantum gravity, 1993. Susskind L. The world as a hologram. Journal of Mathematical Physics 1995;36:6377. Maldacena J. The large N limit of superconformal field theories and supergravity, 1997.

stages.label: The surface holds the volume
stages.text: Working on black holes, 't Hooft and Susskind found that the number of states inside a region scales with its surface area, not its volume. Everything in here can be written on the wall.

stages.label: It became a working tool
stages.text: Maldacena's correspondence turned it into mathematics physicists use daily: a gravitational theory in a volume is exactly equivalent to a theory without gravity on its boundary.

stages.label: And here it stops
stages.text: The step from here to a person surviving is one nobody in this field has taken. The principle is about how many degrees of freedom a region has. It says nothing about whether a self is one of the things conserved.

paths.name: Entanglement, and the microtubule idea
paths.who: Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff, against Max Tegmark
paths.claim: What is established: entanglement is real and was awarded the 2022 Nobel Prize. What is only proposed, and strongly disputed: that the brain uses it, and that what it holds is not local to the brain.
paths.cite: Bell JS. On the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox, 1964. Nobel Prize in Physics 2022: Aspect, Clauser, Zeilinger. Hameroff S, Penrose R. Orchestrated reduction of quantum coherence in brain microtubules, 1996. Tegmark M. Importance of quantum decoherence in brain processes. Physical Review E 2000;61:4194.

stages.label: Two things, one state
stages.text: Entangled particles have no separate states of their own, however far apart they are moved. This is not speculation: it is measured routinely, and the measurements won a Nobel Prize in 2022.

stages.label: The claim about brains
stages.text: Penrose and Hameroff proposed that microtubules inside neurons sustain quantum coherence, and that consciousness is the collapse of it. On their reading, what collapses need not be confined to the skull.

stages.label: The objection
stages.text: Tegmark calculated how long such coherence could survive in a warm wet brain and got around ten million millionths of a second, far too short to matter. The dispute is live, and the hypothesis remains a minority one.

paths.name: The block universe
paths.claim: What is established: in relativity there is no universal present, and the ordering of distant events depends on the observer. What is only proposed: that every moment of a life therefore exists permanently, and nothing is lost when it ends.
paths.cite: Minkowski H. Space and Time, 1908. Einstein's letter to the family of Michele Besso, March 1955, which closes: the distinction between past, present and future is only a stubbornly persistent illusion.

stages.label: No universal now
stages.text: Relativity has no preferred present. Two observers moving differently disagree about which distant events are happening at the same time, and neither of them is wrong.

stages.label: A stubbornly persistent illusion
stages.text: Einstein wrote to the family of his oldest friend, weeks before his own death, that for believing physicists the distinction between past, present and future is only a stubbornly persistent illusion.

stages.label: What it does not promise
stages.text: On this reading a life is not erased, only finished, the way a book is not erased when you stop reading. Note what is missing: nobody is in the block experiencing it. This consoles without surviving anything.

links.name: Four rivers
links.note: Both name exactly four, and three of the four match. Honey, milk, oil and wine in the city of Christ; water, milk, wine and honey in Sura 47.

links.name: The deeds weighed
links.note: A literal pair of scales, in four traditions that did not borrow it from each other: Ani's heart against the feather, the balances heavy or light, Rashn's golden balance, and black pebbles weighed against white.

links.name: The narrow crossing
links.note: The strongest convergence here, and it reaches back into the accounts themselves: Gregory's bridge over the black river, the Chinvat bridge, Tundale's two nailed planks, and as-Sirat.

links.name: Round again
links.note: Three limbs, one shape: death as a turn in a cycle rather than a destination. In Plato's version the soul picks its own next life.

links.name: A garden, not a city
links.note: Where the Christian branch builds architecture, these three plant ground: two gardens, a homestead with wheat and barley, a tank of blue water.

links.name: Nothing is destroyed
links.note: Both reach the same consolation by different routes, and neither delivers a survivor. Nobody is in either of them experiencing anything.
